A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 37 readable pages, including equations, Figures 1–8, references, and Appendices A–C. The material supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulations in Section 4 and Appendix C, plus an original analysis of the labor-supply dataset in Appendix C.6.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation results and labor-supply analysis, including Figures 1–8.

M1.justification: The GD-2SLS updates, transformer architecture, pretraining objective, and coefficient-extraction procedure are unchanged. Replacing t with 0 in Equation (9) matches the input already used in v2's Appendix B.2 proof; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same standard, weak, nonlinear, underdetermined, and multicollinear IV scenarios, varying endogeneity strengths, and the same Alabama labor-supply dataset subset.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain OLS and 2SLS, including their ridge-regularized counterparts in Figure 5b. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain identical experimental settings, including training budgets, model configuration, sample sizes, ICPE and coefficient-MSE metrics, and real-data sampling procedures.

E4.justification: The convergence simulations, instrument-strength and endogeneity-strength sweeps, multicollinearity and nonlinear-IV tests, and labor-supply case study are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix C.

E5.justification: The same figures report averages over 500 simulations, and the labor-supply analysis retains its 500-run boxplot and median estimate. No seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1–8 and the associated empirical findings are unchanged. Appendix C.6 retains labor-supply coefficient estimates of -0.091 for the transformer, -0.089 for 2SLS, and -0.023 for OLS.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 restores the omitted factor ||Θ^(0)−Θ_hat||² in an intermediate bound on ||W^(t)||, correcting a proof inequality. Equation (9) also changes the query-response entry from t to 0. The extensive q²-to-q edits in Theorems 2.1 and 3.3 are algebraically equivalent simplifications: E[||Σ_z^(-1/2)z||²]=q implies K_v2=qK_v3. They do not strengthen the guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about implementing GD-2SLS with transformers, small excess loss, generalization to difficult IV scenarios, and a non-asymptotic 2SLS error bound.

C2.justification: Interpretations of weak-instrument advantages and generalization remain unchanged, as do the boundedness qualification, discussion of the gap between 2SLS and an optimal predictor, and qualifications surrounding the real-data example.

D1.justification: The implementation and data-generation disclosures are unchanged. Section 4.1 and Appendix C.7 retain the same hyperparameters, hardware specifications, and approximately ten-hour training time; no resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, reference list, and novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: The displayed date and arXiv version stamp are updated, with limited notation cleanup. The prose, section order, and narrative structure are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Equation spacing and page layout change locally, especially across Appendices A–B; Appendix B begins one page earlier. Figures 1–8, their captions, axes, legends, and placements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical precision by restoring an omitted factor in Appendix B.1 and aligning Equation (9) with its existing proof. Simplifying K also reduces clutter without strengthening the bounds. These are limited correctness and readability gains; the empirical evidence, main claims, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
